This project is all about requesting, scheduling the tutoring sessions. There are three roles tied to application they are Tutee, Tutor, and Scheduler. A tutee requests for tutoring for the classes that he/she enrolled and gives availability apart from the class timing through Availability Grid and Tutor submits availability. A scheduler will go through those availabilities and schedule time and location for tutoring. Also, there are some set of rules for dropping the tutoring sessions which are incorporated in this project. The other piece of this project is automated emails through Scheduled task which runs every day.

Created a Availability Calendar Grid. In grid each cell represents time (1 hour span) and day of the week. Clicking on the cell toggles the availability. Got rid of data tables and table adapters in the main project as they are tightly coupled. Description:

Summary
Engineer with 8 years in backend and machine learning systems, the last three and a half building the LLM platform of a consumer fintech. - Designed the evaluation harness: 1,200 labelled cases, deterministic checks for tool arguments, LLM-as-judge only for tone, run on every pull request; a regression of more than 2 points blocks the merge.

- Enforced fairness and safety in code, not prompts: a guardrail refuses discriminatory goals before any agent runs, candidates without consent are excluded, agents finish through Pydantic-validated submit tools, and every screening verdict passes a groundedness check.
- Benchmarked the pipeline's four fast decisions (routing, chunk relevance, input guardrail, groundedness) over 170 hand-labelled examples: Jev matched Claude Haiku 4.5 within 3 points while running ~3.5x faster (p50 0.44s vs 1.6s) and ~20x cheaper per decision.
- Both APIs run in Docker Compose; a LiveKit voice agent drives the Interviewer API for live spoken interviews. 104 tests at the public seams, with the model gateway (cost, latency and retries per call) as the only fake.
